clue.text: America guaranteed to be plentiful

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for America
bound to happen means certain or guaranteed

explanation.surface: A boast that America is sure to have plenty of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to exist in large numbers, a straight verb synonym for being plentiful.

clue.text: Football equipment in need of inflation, puff air

parts.words: Football equipment in need of inflation
parts.note: the thing a football match needs, here a flat one waiting to be pumped up
a puff is a piece of promotional praise, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A flat football needs pumping up: puff some air into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puff' and 'air' look like the pumping instructions; 'air' is the definition, a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a simple song or melody, and a ballad is a narrative song, so one is a kind of the other.

clue.text: Waste water keeping streetcar in LA blue

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one word wraps around the rest

parts.note: liquid bodily waste

indicators.note: in places the vehicle inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
streetcar is the American word for a tram

explanation.surface: A grumble about sewage and public transport in Los Angeles making someone feel blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Two wrappings nest here: the city abbreviation holds the vehicle, and the waste word holds both after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultramarine is a deep, vivid shade of blue pigment, so the answer is an example of the colour.

clue.text: Briefly prosper as joiner in the joinery business

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: to prosper is to do well

explanation.surface: A carpentry firm doing well for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'joiner': a carpenter, and also anything that joins two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a wooden peg used by carpenters to fix two pieces of wood together, so it literally joins things in joinery.

clue.text: Russian source coming west as requested

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west means moving right to left, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Red was a common label for a Russian in Soviet times
the root of something is its origin or source

explanation.surface: Information from a Russian informant is defecting westward on demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made to order is made just as requested by the customer, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Fighting in Barking and Kew too

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the words that follow are scrambled crazily

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Reports of brawling in two London districts, Barking and Kew.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking and Kew are both places in London, so 'Barking' reads as a location until it turns out to be the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Taekwondo is a Korean martial art of kicking and punching, a form of combat sport, hence fighting.

clue.text: Books university dons borrowed from the library

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so the books are worn around the university letter

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Academics taking books out of the university library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like a noun for lecturers, but it is the verb meaning puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A library book that is out has been lent and is not on the shelf, a common idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Doctor always takes different view for private route

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so the first pair of words encloses the rest
a different version of the word means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
the four letters of view reordered
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A doctor who always sees things differently on the matter of private healthcare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes' means the first two words together hold the rearranged word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A driveway is a private road leading from a public street to a house, so it is a route on private land.

clue.text: All the pupils perhaps greet sir in order

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them, so they come out rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A classroom of pupils standing in line to greet their teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a school register lists every pupil in the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A class register is the official list of pupils, so the entire class might be described by it.

clue.text: Parking attendant taking so long with Tesla

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A parking attendant saying goodbye as they drive off in a Tesla car.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla reads as the electric car brand, but it is the physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet parks guests' cars at hotels and restaurants, so the word names that kind of attendant.

clue.text: Check trousers first for Superman, underwear going on top

indicators.note: as a verb, to trouser is to pocket something, so the check holds the selected letter

parts.note: to vet is to check carefully

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter, also the emblem on the hero's chest

explanation.surface: A joke about Superman wearing his underpants over his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' is the verb meaning pockets, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest, in British use, is an undershirt, so it is underwear worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Women and others left at home, good for sport

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
the others are the rest
L is the abbreviation for left
someone who is in is at home
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: The women and the rest of the family stay home, good for some sport on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrestling is a competitive combat sport, so the answer is an example of the category.

clue.text: Better protected by largely safe, deep natural harbour

indicators.note: something protected is held inside its guard
largely means most but not all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
to cap is to better or outdo
a deep voice or note is a low one

explanation.surface: A sailor's comment that a deep natural harbour is the safest anchorage.
explanation.walkthrough: Scapa Flow, in Orkney off northern Scotland, was the Royal Navy's main wartime anchorage.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapa Flow is a large sheltered body of water among the Orkney islands, a famous natural harbour.

clue.text: Pair that focuses on bridge design requirements

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pair of spectacles

explanation.surface: Glasses that rest on the bridge of the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' looks like part of the glasses, but it is the engineering structure whose design has specifications.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for both eyeglasses and technical specifications, two unrelated clippings.

clue.text: Cooking pud, son tastes dough

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters that follow are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
licks are little tastes

explanation.surface: A parent cooks a pudding and the son tastes the mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Pud is British slang for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Spondulicks is jokey slang for money, and dough is also slang for cash, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Any video game crashes, run straight after launch

indicators.note: a game that crashes falls into a broken jumble, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gamer's complaint that every video game crashes as soon as it starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launch' and 'run' sound like software, but they refer to a ship being launched and then sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's maiden voyage is its first trip, made right after it is launched into the water.

clue.text: Stop running race that's annoying

parts.note: a dam stops water running
a race of people may be a nation

explanation.surface: An athlete forced to stop mid-race grumbles at the irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is an old-fashioned exclamation of anger or irritation, said when something is annoying.

clue.text: Leave on empty plate a dried-out vegetable

parts.note: to split is slang for to leave

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving just its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child leaving a shrivelled vegetable on an otherwise empty plate.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: A split pea is a dried pea split in half, so it is a vegetable that has been dried out.

clue.text: Engineers quietly broadcast sound again

definitions.note: an adjective phrase; repaired means made sound again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
p is piano, the musical marking for quietly
something aired has been broadcast

explanation.surface: Sound engineers quietly broadcasting audio once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise, but here it means in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repaired has been fixed, so it is in good working order, or sound, once more.

clue.text: Investment vehicle boss cracks before eggheads

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: something that cracks a surface breaks into it and ends up inside

parts.note: great minds are intellectuals
an umbo is the central boss on a shield

explanation.surface: A financial product launched by a boss who cracks under pressure from the intellectuals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not an employer but the raised knob at the centre of a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: Premium Bonds are a British government savings product that pays prizes by lottery, a recognised investment.

clue.text: Graduate cherished last sweet wine

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
a Rolo is a chocolate toffee sweet whose advert asked if you loved someone enough to give them your last one

explanation.surface: A graduate treasures the final dessert wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet wine' looks like one phrase, but 'sweet' belongs to the chocolate and Barolo is a dry red.
explanation.definitionFit: Barolo is a red wine from Piedmont in northern Italy, an example of the broader category.

clue.text: German accommodated by the French supporters

indicators.note: a guest accommodated by a host lives inside the host's home

parts.note: les is the plural form of the in French
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A German guest hosted by a French family.
explanation.definitionFit: Legs hold up a table or a body, so they are things that support, giving a fair whimsical synonym.

clue.text: One's mature look

parts.note: one is, said by the speaker, becomes I am, shortened
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Someone admiring their own grown-up appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a person's appearance or public persona, so it can stand for one's look.

clue.text: Associate a young lady had to listen to

indicators.note: something to be listened to is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a filly is a young female horse, and had a meal means ate

explanation.surface: Talk of a business associate and a young woman they had to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young lady' is a horse here, and 'had' means consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: An affiliate is a member or partner organisation linked to another, so it is an associate.

clue.text: Smoke at home? Criminal, with kids

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: A disapproving question about a criminal smoking at home with children around.
explanation.definitionFit: Fagin is the criminal in Dickens's Oliver Twist who runs a gang of child pickpockets.

clue.text: Rotten PM no good after training

parts.note: PE is physical education
Rishi Sunak was UK Prime Minister from 2022 to 2024
N is an abbreviation for no
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A political jibe that the Prime Minister is rotten and no good after training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you PE comes first, although it is last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Perishing is informal British for wretched or dreadful, and also means decaying, so it is a synonym for rotten.

clue.text: Problem if there's no ring for 10

indicators.note: saying there is no part means that part is taken out

parts.note: the answer at 10-across is a sport, and sumo is the Japanese kind
O is round, like a ring

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what happens to a bout when no ring is available.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 10 is the Japanese version of that sport, minus its round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is an arithmetic problem set to pupils, so it is a type of problem.

clue.text: Short or long pass

definitions.meaning: first meaning: curt or irritable, as in short-tempered
second meaning: in football, a ball played across into the penalty area

explanation.surface: A football coach choosing between a short pass and a long one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross means angry or bad-tempered, like being short with someone, and is also a football term for a pass from the wing.

clue.text: Belly starts twisting in worrying sign

indicators.note: the opening word of the phrase is twisted, so only its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ominous sign is a bad omen

explanation.surface: A twisting pain in the stomach as a worrying symptom.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the start of the phrase, its first word, is jumbled; the rest stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdomen is the part of the body containing the stomach, so it is the belly in anatomical terms.

clue.text: Absentee who's on shifts

indicators.note: shifts means moves around, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A manager checking the rota to see who is on shift and who has not turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is someone who fails to turn up as expected, so they are an absentee.
